title: Harmonica reed
summary: Wailing cupped harmonica, rasp under 3 kHz. One held note over an empty station — the western that answers a man.
notes:
The harmonica that answers the man who plays it — the *Once Upon a Time in the West* sound, one wailing note held over an empty station. A `lead`. **No amp**: the rig's fixed 0.18 power stage is the wrong grit, in the wrong band. A harmonica's rasp is two reeds beating and a cupped hand, both of which are below 3 kHz, and a guitar cab bump sits on top of exactly the frequencies that make it sound like a harp instead of a kazoo.

**A free reed is odd harmonics, so the oscillator is a square.** Manufacturing that spectrum downstream from a sawtooth is the long way round, the same argument the fuzz voices make. Two of them at 9 cents: a ten-hole harp has a blow plate and a draw plate, and they are never in perfect agreement — that slow beating is the instrument's signature and the reason a single clean oscillator reads as an accordion sample.

**Breath is at 0.11, the loudest in the archive, and it belongs at 1.8 kHz.** A harmonica is mostly air: the player is breathing *through* the instrument, so the wind noise is not an onset artifact like a pick click, it is a continuous component sitting right in the middle of the band. Every attempt at this sound that puts the noise up at 4 kHz where a bow lives ends up as a synth lead with hiss on it.

**The hand is the filter, and the hand moves.** Vibrato runs at 6.5 Hz with the archive's widest drift (0.55) at a real depth of 0.05, because harmonica vibrato is produced by opening and closing a cupped hand and by the throat — mechanically irregular in a way a string player's is not. On the real instrument some of that wobble is timbre rather than pitch; this rig has no amplitude LFO, so the pitch modulation carries it, which is an approximation and worth knowing about.

`body` is the comb and the cup: 500 Hz and 1700 Hz lifted, a narrow 2.9 kHz honk, and −6 dB at 5 kHz. That last one matters — a harmonica has no sparkle at all, the reeds simply stop producing up there, and any air above 5 kHz reads as a melodica.

The envelope is 30 ms in (a reed has mass and takes air to start moving), 0.85 sustain (it holds as long as the breath does), and only 0.18 s out, because closing the hand or stopping the breath kills the reed almost instantly. Polyphony 4 — chords are possible on a harp and the low chugging ones are half of the style.
